ARC-REV-01.rationale: The new domain rules sit in Tier 2. These are the schema and version checks, the record and invariant checks on import, the data-version match, the 'only into new books' rule, and the GitHub refusal. They are in Summa.Storage.Transfer and Summa.Web.Engine.Accounting. The Tier 3 wire only maps kernel event names to engine messages and re-decides nothing.

evidence.quote: match Transfer.export manifest books ctx.Now with

ARC-REV-02.rationale: Transfer is pure and takes exportedAt as a parameter. The engine gets the time from the message context (`ctx.Now`) and requests the download as an `OfferDownload` effect, as data. The save after import goes through the existing `save` helper. No clock, I/O or randomness is added below Tier 4.

evidence.quote: let private githubTransferSentence = "Books on GitHub are moved with their repository, not with a transfer file."

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Each new fact has one definition and is referenced from both uses: the schema, the version, the GitHub sentence, the classification (taken from `Exports.Classification`) and the data version (taken from `Exports.dataVersion`). The only restatement I can see is the 'This browser cannot offer downloads here.' literal at Accounting.fs line 230. The requirement describes it as an existing error, so it is probably already present elsewhere, but the diff doesn't show that. Any copy would agree in text.

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The counts, the contents-versus-books check and the version 1/2 acceptance are decided in Tier 2 (Summa.Storage.Transfer). The preview is projected in the Tier 2 engine view by calling `Transfer.read`. No Tier 3 or Tier 4 code is added that re-derives any of it. The HTML change is only a binding.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no effect. The preview is a pure view projection over the pasted text, and `Transfer.read` stays pure. Nothing is read from a clock, I/O or randomness.

evidence.quote: | Error why -> $"This file cannot be imported: {why}"
| Some n when n <> 1m && n <> decimal Version ->

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The counts have one definition, `contentsOf`, and both export and read use it. Three things are restated, and all of them agree for now. First, the 'This file cannot be imported: …' prefix is written in `transferPreview` and again in the `BooksTransferImported` handler from change set 1. Second, the export-date derivation is written in the preview and again in the import notice. Third, the accepted version 1 is a bare `1m` literal next to `Version`, and read also repeats `n = 1m`. None of these can contradict the others today, but each can drift.
